title: Readers’ Rides: Carlo’s Cascada x Massacan Pianella MTB
content:
For this week’s Readers’ Rides, we have a follow-up to John’s Shop Visit with Massacan in Nice, France, and that special one-of-one Pianella frame painted for Italian apparel company Cascada. Read on Carlo from Cascada’s words on this special Pianella MTB collaboration…

I wanted to send you our custom Cascada x Massacan Pianella for Readers’ Rides.

Funny enough, you already saw the frame before we did :-) When you visited Lucie, Matt and the Massacan crew in Nice this summer, the freshly painted Cascada frame was there with them, so you had a first look at it before it even made its way back to us in Italy.

The story behind the bike actually started a few years earlier.

At the end of 2022, French illustrator Denis Carrier, a longtime collaborator of Cascada, who has designed several graphics for us over the years, introduced us to Lucie and Massacan, which at the time was still a young project taking shape in the South of France.

Lucie got in touch while they were preparing the launch of their first bikes. The idea was simple: head out on a multi-day bikepacking trip between France and Italy and involve Cascada in the project.

Their bikes were being welded and painted in Italy, not far from Lake Garda, where we live, and the connection felt immediate.

My answer at the time was basically: count on us.

At Cascada, we’ve always been drawn to collaborations that start from the ground up: projects where two independent brands can ride together, create something together and grow alongside each other, rather than simply place two logos on the same product.

That first email became the beginning of a friendship and an ongoing collaboration.

Over the following years, Massacan bikes found their way to our part of the Italian Alps, where we rode them through our mountains, forests and trails. We worked together on photo shoots, trips and projects, while Denis Carrier also designed Cascada x Massacan Trail T-shirts and bandanas.

Last May, we spent two days together in Val di Ledro (North Italy), for The Lodge Dispatch, an event we organized around the presentation of our SS2026 collection. We stayed at a lodge deep in the woods, rode together, introduced the Pianella and the rest of the Massacan bikes to the Italian cycling community and shared the new Cascada collection in the same setting.

Before the event, Lucie and Matt came to us with an idea: they asked if we wanted to design a Cascada graphic for a Pianella frame and make the bike ours.

It was an easy yes.

The finished bike was then delivered to us during the event in Val di Ledro.

The result is this Massacan Pianella, assembled for us by Matt at Massacan and finished with a custom paint job by Tony Spray.

The Pianella is an adventure hardtail: Massacan’s first mountain bike and its first steel frame, built around Columbus Zona tubing. For ours, we chose a rigid Columbus Futura Adventure carbon fork and a simple, capable build suited to the kind of riding we do most: forest trails, mountain tracks, long days outside and the occasional bikepacking trip.

What makes this one particularly personal is the frame.

We designed the complete graphic treatment ourselves at Cascada and asked Tony Spray to bring it to life. Rather than creating a conventional co-branded paint scheme, we treated the frame almost like a blank canvas.

The sand, olive and burnt-orange palette comes directly from the colors and landscapes surrounding Cascada. Across the frame we added symbols that have become part of our visual language over the years: the moon, the sun, the snake, wildlife and the words Stay Wild.

They are small references to the things that have always shaped Cascada: mountains, forests, rivers, travelling slowly and the ongoing search for unknown places.

Even the bike carries traces of the relationship behind it: Cascada x Massacan on the top tube, Massacan’s handwritten Pianella lettering and Tony Spray’s signature on the frame.

For us, it’s much more than a custom-painted bike.

It’s probably the clearest physical expression of everything that grew out of that first email in 2022: French ideas, Italian craftsmanship, independent brands, shared rides and a lot of time spent together on dirt roads.

And, most importantly, it’s a bike that gets ridden.

Build Spec:

  • Frame: Massacan Pianella — Columbus Zona steel
  • Fork: Columbus Futura Adventure carbon
  • Assembly: Matt / Massacan
  • Custom paint: Tony Spray
  • Rear derailleur: Shimano Deore XT RD-M8100, 12-speed
  • Cassette: Shimano Deore XT CS-M8100, 12-speed
  • Brakes: Shimano Deore XT M8100 hydraulic disc
  • Wheelset: Miche 988 WHS, 29″
  • Hubs: Miche
  • Tires: Vittoria Barzo XC-Trail, 29 x 2.25″
  • Handlebar: Ritchey Trail
  • Stem: Ritchey
  • Seatpost: Crankbrothers dropper
  • Saddle: Selle San Marco Mantra
  • Pedals: Shimano PD-ED500 SPD
  • Bottle cages: Ritchey Classic Steel

See more of the Pianella at Massacan.
